channel.title: Neurolopedia
channel.description: Stories, news and explanations of the headlines about the brain and neurological disease, without jargon.

item.title: A blood test for Alzheimer's: what it detects and when it helps
item.description: New blood tests help find out whether memory problems are due to Alzheimer's disease. They are a major advance, but they are not a test to have out of curiosity.

item.title: How Neurolopedia began
item.description: An encyclopedia about the brain and nervous system, their diseases, tests and treatments, first written in Spanish and now also in English, with sources on every page.

item.title: Fourteen factors to protect your memory
item.description: The Lancet Commission estimates that almost half of all dementia cases could be prevented or delayed by acting on fourteen risk factors. What they are and what to do at each stage of life.

item.title: Cajal, the cover photo
item.description: The image at the top of Neurolopedia is a portrait of Santiago Ramón y Cajal, the scientist who showed that the brain is made of neurons. The story behind him.

item.title: 29 October, World Stroke Day
item.description: One in four people will have a stroke in their lifetime. Recognising it and calling the emergency number within the first few minutes changes the outlook.
